thread:
Rohan: Quick follow-up from the probe-token incident yesterday. We need a stronger handoff between admission and runtime for abuse scoring + tenant weights.
Priya: I saw the spike. The probe tokens had no tenant_priority meta so the fairness layer treated them like normal traffic.
Alex: Right, that caused the soft-eviction to evict the wrong queue. We should surface a numeric 'abuse_score' and a 'tenancy_weight' in the admission request/response.
Taylor: Proposal: admission offers tokens with these attrs: {tokens, window_ms, abuse_score, weight_label}. Runtimes must include the weight_label in scheduling decisions.
Rohan: Example sketch:```json
admission_request: { tenant_id: "t-123", req_tokens: 50, runtime_caps: { can_degrade: true } }
admit_response: { decision: "ADMIT", tokens: 30, abuse_score: 0.7, weight_label: "W2" }
```
Priya: We need to define weight_label semantics. Suggest labels W0..W4 mapped to numeric multipliers in the fairness layer (W0=0.1, W4=2.0). Mapping stored in eng-platform config and versioned.
Alex: Important: abuse_score should be bounded [0,1] and must be treated as probabilistic, not binary. Schedulers should combine abuse_score and weight multipliers to compute drain priority.
Taylor: Edge case: background batch jobs pinned to low-latency GPU pools. If they get a high abuse_score due to probe traffic, they could be starved. Add an immutable "pin" flag in tenant metadata that admission respects. If pinned, enforce min_tokens.
Rohan: Also want the admission API to carry a 'probe_kind' enum so runtimes can special-case probes vs customer traffic. probe_kind: LIVE_EVAL | SYNTHETIC_HEALTH | PROBE.
Priya: Telemetry: emit admission.{tenant,region,abuse_score,weight_label,probe_kind,decision} with a 0.01 sample rate for high-cardinality fields. Record hint acceptance separately.
Alex: For abuse prevention, we should add a backstop: when abuse_score > 0.9, admission can return REJECT and add `abuse_reason` short code for debugging.
Taylor: We must avoid leaking PII or sensitive signals. abuse_reason should be high-level enums only. Eg: ABUSIVE_RATE, STOLEN_KEY, MALFORMED_PAYLOAD. No raw signatures.
Rohan: Migration: 1) deploy schema v2 with optional fields; 2) publish label->multiplier mapping; 3) enable for canary tenants (feature-flag); 4) after 7 days of canary, widen scope.
Priya: Who owns the mapping? eng-platform owns registry; eng-runtime teams must read mapping periodically (ttl cache).
Alex: Note on caching: runtime cache TTL should be small (1m) so we can adjust weights without full deploy. But add jitter to avoid thundering herd.
Taylor: Security: any tenant-supplied pin / override must be validated server-side. Don't trust client runtime claims.
Rohan: Tests: need simulation harness to re-run last week's traffic with new abuse_score logic and weight multipliers to measure fairness delta.
Priya: I'll add a sim job to perf infra.
Alex: UI: Console wants a "weight_label" column and a heatmap for abuse_score over time. Product will follow up.
deploy-bot: Feature flag created: eng-platform.probe-abuse-handshake scoped to us-east-1 and 5% traffic.
Taylor: Implementation split: Rohan -> admission service + registry, Priya -> telemetry & sim, Alex -> scheduler changes in runtime, Taylor -> console cell + docs.
Rohan: I'll draft the RFC update outlining types, enums, telemetry, ownership and roll plan. Post in #eng-platform tomorrow morning.
Priya: One last thought: add a 'suggested_backoff_ms' in the response so clients and SDKs can smooth retry storms.
Alex: Good call. That will help reduce tight retry loops and secondary cascading failures.
Rohan: Cool. We're aligned. I'll follow up with the RFC link and an initial proto PR.
